title: Clear four glasses with ice and straws into a bus tub in one trip, two pinched together in each gripper
instruction: Clear the four glasses from the table into the bus tub in one trip: each hand goes to the tub only once.
context: Clearing dirty glasses is daily work for waiters and waitresses (2,284,400 US jobs), bartenders (762,600) and dining room and cafeteria attendants and bartender helpers (546,600): 3.59 million jobs (BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, 2025 employment). O*NET 35-3031: "Remove dishes and glasses from tables or counters, and take them to kitchen for cleaning." One glass per hand per trip is too slow for a shift ("full hands in, full hands out"), so several go in each hand, commonly with a finger down inside each dirty glass and the walls pinched together. Glasses left with ice and a straw do not nest. A parallel gripper cannot close round two glasses, so this pinch is how it takes two: they must first be brought rim to rim, pushed low so they slide and do not tip, and then hang from two 2.5 mm walls while lifted over a tub wall nearly as tall as they are.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x away from the robot, y to its left; heights above the table. A light grey polyethylene bus tub (20 x 15 x 5 in class: 50.6 x 38.9 cm over its rim, 12.5 cm tall, 0.64 kg, inside 43.2 x 32.1 cm at the floor and 11.7 cm deep, walls leaning out about 11 degrees) stands loose on the table, centred at (37.0, 0), its long side along x. Four 16 oz stackable pebbled SAN plastic restaurant tumblers (blue; rim 82.6 mm, base 60.3 mm, 138 mm tall, 2.5 mm wall, 85 g) stand upright on the table outside the tub's long walls, two on each side in a row along x with 10.0 cm between their rims: centres at (22.0, 32.0) and (40.3, 32.0) on the left, (22.0, -32.0) and (40.3, -32.0) on the right. Each holds three reusable plastic ice cubes (25.4 mm, 13 g each) and one 7 3/4 in paper straw (197 x 6 mm, 1.3 g) that stands on its floor and leans on its rim on the side away from the tub. A filled tumbler weighs 125 g. Nothing else is on the table; both grippers start open at the ready pose. The screenshot shows the start.
scoring:
Read at the end of the run from the tub, the table and the video. Delivered: a tumbler standing on the tub's floor within 15 degrees of upright (no more than 2 cm between the high and low sides of its rim, by ruler), at rest, with its three ice cubes and its straw inside it (a count). One trip: no gripper carried tumblers in over the tub's rim more than once (from the video; tumblers that pass over the rim in the same gripper within 1 s of each other are one carry), every tumbler in the tub was carried in by a gripper, and no tumbler was put inside another at any time.
0: any tumbler was knocked over (more than 45 degrees from upright) at any time, even if stood up again; anything fell off the table; an ice cube or a straw ends up lying outside the tub and outside every tumbler; or fewer than two tumblers are delivered.
0.25: two or three tumblers delivered.
0.5: all four delivered, but not in one trip, or a gripper is still within 6 cm of a tumbler, or something was still moving in the last 1 s.
1.0: all four delivered in one trip, both grippers 6 cm or more from every tumbler, and tumblers and grippers still for 1 s (the simulated trial ends once this has held for 0.5 s).
The tub may slide; everything is judged relative to the tub where it ends. Simulation: the same readings from the bodies' poses; a tumbler counts as carried by a gripper whose fingertip midpoint is within 12 cm of its rim's centre as its base passes over the rim.
reset_notes: Stand the four tumblers back on their marks with three ice cubes and a straw in each, the straw leaning away from the tub, and set the tub back on its outline. Nothing is consumed. Use plastic ice cubes, not ice, so that nothing melts between trials.
fidelity: Rigid-body contact and friction only; nothing is attached to a gripper. Tumblers are true size and hollow: 24 flat wall panels 2.5 mm thick on a floor disc; the pebbled surface and rounded rim are not modelled. Friction 0.45 tumbler on table and on finger pads (real pads grip better), 0.4 tumbler on tumbler. The tub is a loose rigid box with leaning walls and a flat lip, no handles or rounded corners. No leftover drink: the ice and straw stand in for what spills. Plastic does not chip.
